newsitem.title: USA: US WCoast crudes turn mixed as ANS discount widens.
newsitem.headline: US WCoast crudes turn mixed as ANS discount widens.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes turned mixed late Wednesday, with Line 63 lifted by West Texas Intermediate (WTI), while Alaska North Slope eased after a cheaper deal got done between Texaco and Exxon.
Discounts for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude slipped from $2.15 a barrel last Friday to $2.25 late today after Texaco bought a full cargo for October delivery off October WTI.
Buyers had earlier dropped their bids as low as $2.30 with talk they could widen to $2.50.
WTI reached $24.70/24.80 a barrel, supported by higher futures prices that came on the heels of U.S./Iraq tensions.
A major Northwest refinery claimed to have sold Kern River heavy crude at postings.
Kern River was quoted at discounts of around 75/25 cents to posted pricings at $15.75 a barrel.
But one trader discounted the rumors, citing sales of heavy crudes into the fuel oil market as evidence the market remained oversupplied.
Values for Wilmington stood at $17.00/17.20 a barrel, while Line 63 differentials were unchanged at WTI minus $2.60/2.50 a barrel.
